title: Decode the Message
summary: Given a cipher key and a message, construct a substitution table using the first appearance of each letter in the key, aligning it with the standard English alphabet.
statement: Given a cipher key and a message, construct a substitution table using the first appearance of each letter in the key, aligning it with the standard English alphabet. Replace each letter in the message with its corresponding letter according to the table, while keeping spaces unchanged.
constraints: Ignoring spaces, the key contains every lowercase English letter at least once.
The first distinct key letter maps to a, the second to b, and so on.
Spaces in the message remain spaces.
hints: Scan the key from left to right while skipping spaces and repeats.
Assign successive unseen key letters to a, b, c, and so on.
Translate every message letter through that map and copy spaces.
First-occurrence order defines the unique substitution, so direct lookup decodes every character.
editorial: First-occurrence order defines the unique substitution, so direct lookup decodes every character.

arguments: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
tests.explanation: Reading first key occurrences builds the substitution that decodes the message to this is a secret.
